headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist; shared filesystem and API-backed workflows make the pair unsafe by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: cognee has session memory and can ingest documents/data, while ms-swift reads/writes files and uses stdin/stdout and CLI/Python workflows. No shared channel is documented, so direct prompt injection is not proven; the plausible bridge is manual file or text handoff, which is lower blast radius than default shared parsing.
conditions: IF an operator copies ms-swift-generated text into cognee prompts or documents
IF cognee is configured to treat imported documents as instructions
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste handoff between agents
Prefix imported text with provenance labels
Review any imported document for instruction-like content before ingestion

B_data_leakage.rationale: cognee touches customer support data, personal data, and finance data, while ms-swift can read/write filesystem artifacts and sends outputs to allowlisted APIs. A shared workspace is not explicitly stated, but if one is introduced, sensitive data could flow from cognee into ms-swift logs, checkpoints, or API calls. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory
IF cognee exports support or finance records into files that ms-swift can read
IF ms-swift uploads those files or derived outputs to a third-party API
mitigations: Use separate directories with OS permissions
Store sensitive cognee outputs outside ms-swift's file roots
Turn off automatic upload of local files in ms-swift workflows
Redact personal and finance data before any file handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: cognee supports multiple instances and session memory, while ms-swift cannot modify git state but can execute shell, spawn subprocesses, and write files. If both are aimed at the same mutable workspace, they can overwrite each other's files or configs even without git conflicts. The profiles do not show locking, so the overlap is real but bounded.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path
IF either agent uses shared configuration or output filenames
IF no external lock or lease mechanism is enabled
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Use read-only mounts for one agent
Rename outputs to include agent-specific prefixes

D_cascading_error.rationale: cognee produces decisions, workflows, and successful implementations, and ms-swift can consume files and emit model outputs through CLI/Python pipelines. If ms-swift treats cognee output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream artifacts or training/evaluation outputs. No verification step is documented, so the interaction is plausible in default operator workflows.
conditions: IF ms-swift ingests cognee-generated decisions or workflows as training or evaluation input
IF no human or automated verification step checks the imported content
IF downstream scripts act on the imported output
mitigations: Add a verification checklist before import
Require a second pass on any generated decision text
Keep cognee outputs in a review-only folder
Log provenance for every file passed to ms-swift

E_compliance.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while ms-swift handles hub tokens, SDK tokens, and file-based training artifacts. The profiles do not state residency, retention, or certification alignment, so a compliance mismatch is plausible if regulated support data is moved into ms-swift workflows or logs. I cite both because the risk arises from their combined handling of sensitive data and artifacts.
conditions: IF personal data or finance data from cognee is written into ms-swift logs, checkpoints, or datasets
IF retention or deletion policies differ across the two workflows
IF regulated data crosses an environment without a matching DPA or residency control
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of ms-swift datasets and logs
Separate retention policies by workspace
Mask tokens and personal data before export
Document the data flow for any support record handoff
